content.text: surg delayed until HTN controlled w α- + BBs, USU phenoxybenzamine 20 to 40 mg PO TID; BP target < 130/80; blockade presumed effective after ~10 to 14 days (CV re-equilibration); intraop hypertensive paroxysms: phentolamine 1 to 5 mg IV or nitroprusside infusion
Initially 10 mg BID. Increase QOD, USU to 20 to 40 mg 2 or TID, until optimal (BP control). Start sm & ↑ slowly until desired effect or side effects from blockade become troublesome

CI: conditions where a fall in BP may be undesirable - hypersensitivity to the drug or any components. α blockade leaves β receptors unopposed - compounds that stim both receptor types may prod an exaggerated hypotensive response & tachy. May interact w Epi to prod an exaggerated hypotensive response & tachy. Case reports of carcinoma in humans after long-term tx - long-term use ⍉recommended. Use w caution in marked cerebral or coronary arteriosclerosis or renal damage - blocking effect may aggravate Sx of resp infect. Adverse rxns: postural hypotension · tachy · inhibition of ejaculation · nasal congestion · miosis. OD Sx: postural hypotension w dizziness or fainting · tachy (esp postural) · vomiting · lethargy · shock. OD tx: d/c drug - tx of circulatory failure = prime consideration. Epi = contraindicated in OD (net effect = vasodilate & further drop in BP: Epi reversal). IV levarterenol bitartrate may be used for severe hypotensive rxns (stimulates α-receptors primarily)
